summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Builds native C++ desktop applications with Qt-family GUI frameworks (PySide6) and OpenGL-backed 3D visualization, including a from-scratch SE(3) transform engine for coordinate-frame rendering. Comfortable across CMake-based C++ build systems, CUDA kernel optimization, and MPI parallel programming, with hands-on experience debugging and profiling native software on Linux.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: Frame Simulator — Desktop 3D Coordinate-Frame Visualizer
bullets: Built a PySide6/Qt desktop GUI with an OpenGL-backed VisPy 3D viewport to visualize coordinate-frame hierarchies, parent-child transform chains, and SE(3) poses in real time.

Wrote a custom DSL parser and SE(3) math engine (math_se3.py) supporting local/world rotation and translation composition, recursive world-transform chaining, and live 4x4 matrix inspection per frame.
Decoupled data model, math, visuals, and UI into separate modules with a mix-in pattern centralizing transform-apply, matrix-refresh, and animation logic.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and a 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on physical UR5e via UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms (uncoalesced) and 77.5ms (CPU TorchScript) — ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000×5000 pixel scenes using MPI.
Achieved up to 30× speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); demonstrated dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
